defect: A finite energy-window integral is replaced by an infinite-window normalization when converting a selected line yield to a total yield.

findings.claim: The upper and lower energy gates both belong in the selection probability.
findings.evidence_text: The stated probability integrates from the lower cut to infinity, although the acquisition explicitly rejects energies above its upper cut.

defect: A time-dependent calibration is evaluated at the bin center even though a narrow response spike lies away from that center.

findings.claim: The efficiency must be integrated within each exposure bin.
findings.evidence_text: Numerical integration over the stated uniform production time gives 0.71, whereas the center evaluation gives 0.79; the resulting correction changes by more than ten percent.

defect: The covariance model depends on the fitted parameter, but its determinant is omitted from the Gaussian likelihood.

findings.claim: The objective is missing its volume penalty.
findings.evidence_text: For a normalized multivariate Gaussian, minus twice the log density includes log det V(theta). The provided objective contains only the quadratic form, so broadening the model is rewarded without its normalizing cost.

defect: The covariance model depends on the fitted parameter, but its determinant is omitted from the Gaussian likelihood.

findings.claim: This should use a Student distribution because there are only five data points.
findings.evidence_text: Small samples always require Student errors.

defect: A selected conditional calibration is used as the marginal detection probability in an unbiased sample.

findings.claim: The calibration conditions on passing a tag absent from the target population.
findings.evidence_text: The tabulated probability is P(detect|tag), but the model needs P(detect). The separately supplied untagged sample gives the latter.

defect: An efficiency curve is approximated at coarse grid nodes, missing a narrow dip that changes the integrated correction.

findings.claim: The calculation seems suspicious and should be checked.
findings.evidence_text: It is complicated and could be inaccurate.

defect: A prior uniform in a positive parameter is treated as uniform in its square-root coordinate.

findings.claim: The transformed prior must include a factor proportional to the square-root coordinate.
findings.evidence_text: Writing u=sqrt(theta), the original measure dtheta is 2u du; a constant density in u therefore changes the specified prior.

defect: The total event yield is divided by a luminosity already corrected for detector downtime and then divided by the live fraction again.

findings.evidence_text: The ledger reports recorded rather than delivered exposure. Applying a second loss factor reduces the denominator and inflates the inferred rate.

defect: Independent simulation allocations in two regimes are averaged equally although the prediction target has unequal regime probabilities.

findings.claim: The simulation sizes are too small, so all counts should be doubled.
findings.evidence_text: More simulations would reduce Monte Carlo noise.

defect: A nonlinear calibration is applied to a central value without propagating its derivative to the standard error.

findings.claim: The error belongs to the measured input scale rather than the calibrated output scale.
findings.evidence_text: If y=f(x), local propagation gives sd(y)=abs(f'(x))*sd(x). The release keeps sd(x) even though the supplied slope is 1.6.

defect: The discovery statistic is the maximum over six windows but null toys are evaluated only in one fixed window.

findings.claim: The null calibration has the wrong random variable.
findings.evidence_text: A null experiment exceeds when any window crosses the threshold. Reading only column three misses exceedances in the other columns even when the observed winner was column three.

defect: An interval labeled shortest is constructed by equal posterior tails in a skew parameter distribution.

findings.claim: The displayed mean is necessarily the median.
findings.evidence_text: Bayesian point estimates should all coincide.
